findings.current: You can never be my equal.
findings.defect: The Korean says he can never be the Blood Lord’s match or opponent, not that he can never be his equal. That changes a claim about fighting ability into one about status.
findings.rationale: 네놈은 결코 내 상대가 될 수 없어 means the addressee cannot contend with him; it does not establish inequality in rank or standing.
findings.replacement: You can never be a match for me.

findings.defect: “Taishan” without “Mount” can read as the established character name, rather than the mountain image in the Korean simile.
findings.rationale: 태산과도 같은 기세 compares the monster’s force or momentum to a great mountain. The accepted baseline preserved that image as “Mount Taishan.”
findings.replacement: with the momentum of Mount Taishan.

summary: Mostly faithful. Two lines shift the meaning or image of the Korean source.
